title: Improve error handling in ByteToMessageDecoder when expand fails

timeline.body:
Motivation:

The buffer which the decoder allocates for the expansion can be
leaked if there is a subsequent issue writing to it.

Modifications:
The error handling has been improved so that the new buffer always
is released on failure in the expand.

Result:
The decoder will not leak in this scenario any more.

Fixes: https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/9812
Can one of the admins verify this patch?
why we need this change ? Can we not just extend `AbstractByteBufAllocator` ?

reply.body: I am sure we can, I'm not too used to fiddling in this code base. Let me take a deeper look.

timeline.body:
Thanks @martinfurmanski ... looks good to me but I thought of another simplification, WDYT?

I'm also now wondering whether the try/finally error handling should be outside that method so that it spans all of the cumulator logic... since it would be easy to introduce a similar bug later i.e. if anything nontrivial was done in the cumulator after calling this method.

> I'm also now wondering whether the try/finally error handling should be outside that method so that it spans all of the cumulator logic... since it would be easy to introduce a similar bug later i.e. if anything nontrivial was done in the cumulator after calling this method.

I generally agree, but I don't want to change too much. As it stands it seems fairly easy to reason about equivalence and correctness.
you will need to call `newCumulation.release();` as well to ensure we not leak buffers in the test

reply.body: Oh ok! I assumed it wasn't necessary because it was from the unpooled heap and the test I started from didn't attempt to clean it up before. Will fix!

timeline.body: you will need to call `oldCumulation.release();` as well to ensure we not leak buffers in the test
sorry missed this before... You also need to call `oldCumulation .release()` here

reply.body: Yea sorry from me as well, should have noticed.
